sentences.zh: 夏殷已上，左史記言，右史記事，周則太史、小史、內史、外史、御史，分掌其事，而諸侯之國，亦置史官。

translations.literal: From the Xia and Yin dynasties upward, the left scribe recorded speech and the right scribe recorded events. Under Zhou the Grand Scribe, Junior Scribe, Internal Scribe, External Scribe, and Imperial Censor divided these duties among themselves, and the states of the feudal lords likewise appointed historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xia and Yin dynasties upward, the left scribe recorded speech and the right scribe recorded events. Under Zhou the Grand Scribe, Junior Scribe, Internal Scribe, External Scribe, and Imperial Censor divided these duties among themselves, and the states of the feudal lords likewise appointed historiographers.

sentences.zh: 又《春秋國語》引周志、鄭書之說，推尋事蹟，似當時記事，各有職司，後又合而撰之，總成書記。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Discourses of the States and the Spring and Autumn cite the chronicles of Zhou and the documents of Zheng; tracing the events, it seems that record-keeping at the time was assigned to separate offices, and that these were later combined and compiled into comprehensive historical writings.
translations.idiomatic: The Discourses of the States and the Spring and Autumn cite the chronicles of Zhou and the documents of Zheng; tracing the events, it seems that record-keeping at the time was assigned to separate offices, and that these were later combined and compiled into comprehensive historical writings.

sentences.zh: 其後陵夷衰亂，史官放絕，秦滅先王之典，遺制莫存。

translations.literal: Afterward the realm declined into disorder and the historiographers were abolished; Qin destroyed the institutions of the former kings, and no trace of the old system remained.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the realm declined into disorder and the historiographers were abolished; Qin destroyed the institutions of the former kings, and no trace of the old system remained.

sentences.zh: 至漢武帝時，始置太史公，命司馬談為之，以掌其職。

translations.literal: It was not until the reign of Emperor Wu of Han that the office of Grand Historian was first established and Sima Tan was appointed to it to oversee its duties.
translations.idiomatic: It was not until the reign of Emperor Wu of Han that the office of Grand Historian was first established and Sima Tan was appointed to it to oversee its duties.

sentences.zh: 時天下計書，皆先上太史，副上丞相，遺文古事，靡不畢臻。

translations.literal: At that time all provincial reports from throughout the realm were first sent to the Grand Historian and a copy to the Chancellor; surviving texts and ancient events—none failed to reach them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time all provincial reports from throughout the realm were first sent to the Grand Historian and a copy to the Chancellor; surviving texts and ancient events—none failed to reach them.

sentences.zh: 談乃據《左氏》、《國語》、《世本》、《戰國策》、《楚漢春秋》，接其後事，成一家之言。

translations.literal: Tan then drew upon the Mr. Zuo, the Discourses of the States, the Genealogical Records, the Intrigues of the Warring States, and the Annals of Chu and Han, continuing the narrative from where they left off to form a school of history in his own right.
translations.idiomatic: Tan then drew upon the Mr. Zuo, the Discourses of the States, the Genealogical Records, the Intrigues of the Warring States, and the Annals of Chu and Han, continuing the narrative from where they left off to form a school of history in his own right.

sentences.zh: 談卒，其子遷又為太史令，嗣成其志。

translations.literal: When Tan died, his son Qian also became Grand Historian and carried on his father's design.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan died, his son Qian also became Grand Historian and carried on his father's design.

sentences.zh: 上自黃帝，訖於炎漢，合十二本紀、十表、八書、三十世家、七十列傳，謂之《史記》。

translations.literal: Beginning with the Yellow Emperor and ending with the Han dynasty, it comprised twelve basic annals, ten tables, eight treatises, thirty hereditary houses, and seventy arrayed biographies—this work was called the Records of the Grand Historian.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning with the Yellow Emperor and ending with the Han dynasty, it comprised twelve basic annals, ten tables, eight treatises, thirty hereditary houses, and seventy arrayed biographies—this work was called the Records of the Grand Historian.

sentences.zh: 遷卒以後，好事者亦頗著述，然多鄙淺，不足相繼。

translations.literal: After Qian's death, enthusiasts also wrote histories in considerable number, but most were shallow and unworthy to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: After Qian's death, enthusiasts also wrote histories in considerable number, but most were shallow and unworthy to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 至後漢扶風班彪，綴後傳數十篇，並譏正前失。

translations.literal: In Later Han, Ban Biao of Fufeng appended several dozen chapters of continuation and also criticized errors in the earlier work.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han, Ban Biao of Fufeng appended several dozen chapters of continuation and also criticized errors in the earlier work.

sentences.zh: 彪卒，明帝命其子固續成其志。

translations.literal: When Biao died, Emperor Ming ordered his son Gu to continue and complete his father's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao died, Emperor Ming ordered his son Gu to continue and complete his father's intent.

sentences.zh: 以為唐、虞、三代，世有典籍，史遷所記，乃以漢氏繼于百王之末，非其義也。

translations.literal: He held that the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties each had their own canonical records, whereas what Sima Qian recorded placed the Han dynasty after the hundred kings—this was not the proper principle.
translations.idiomatic: He held that the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties each had their own canonical records, whereas what Sima Qian recorded placed the Han dynasty after the hundred kings—this was not the proper principle.

sentences.zh: 故斷自高祖，終於孝平、王莽之誅，為十二紀、八表、十志、六十九傳。

translations.literal: Therefore he began with Emperor Gaozu and ended with the execution of Emperor Ping and Wang Mang, producing twelve annals, eight tables, ten treatises, and sixty-nine biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he began with Emperor Gaozu and ended with the execution of Emperor Ping and Wang Mang, producing twelve annals, eight tables, ten treatises, and sixty-nine biographies.

translations.literal: He devoted himself to the work with concentrated thought for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to the work with concentrated thought for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 建初中，始奏表及紀傳，其十志竟不能就。

translations.literal: In the early Jianchu era he first submitted his memorial together with the annals and biographies, but the ten treatises were never completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jianchu era he first submitted his memorial together with the annals and biographies, but the ten treatises were never completed.

sentences.zh: 固卒後，始命曹大家續成之。

translations.literal: After Gu's death, the court at last ordered Madame Cao to continue and complete the work.
translations.idiomatic: After Gu's death, the court at last ordered Madame Cao to continue and complete the work.

sentences.zh: 先是明帝召固為蘭台令史，與諸先輩陳宗、尹敏、孟冀等，共成《光武本紀》。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Ming had summoned Gu to serve as Clerk of the Orchid Terrace; together with senior scholars Chen Zong, Yin Min, Meng Ji, and others, they completed the Basic Annals of Emperor Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Ming had summoned Gu to serve as Clerk of the Orchid Terrace; together with senior scholars Chen Zong, Yin Min, Meng Ji, and others, they completed the Basic Annals of Emperor Guangwu.

translations.literal: Gu was promoted to Gentleman and put in charge of collating the secret archives.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was promoted to Gentleman and put in charge of collating the secret archives.

sentences.zh: 固撰後漢事，作《列傳載記》二十八篇。

translations.literal: Gu compiled events of Later Han and produced twenty-eight chapters of Biographical Records and Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Gu compiled events of Later Han and produced twenty-eight chapters of Biographical Records and Annals.

sentences.zh: 其後劉珍、劉毅、劉陶、伏無忌等，相次著述東觀，謂之《漢記》。

translations.literal: Thereafter Liu Zhen, Liu Yi, Liu Tao, Fu Wuji, and others wrote in succession at the Eastern Pavilion; their work was called the Records of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Liu Zhen, Liu Yi, Liu Tao, Fu Wuji, and others wrote in succession at the Eastern Pavilion; their work was called the Records of Han.

sentences.zh: 及三國鼎峙，魏氏及吳，並有史官。

translations.literal: When the Three Kingdoms stood in tripartite rivalry, Wei as well as Wu each had historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Kingdoms stood in tripartite rivalry, Wei as well as Wu each had historiographers.

sentences.zh: 晉時，巴西陳壽刪集三國之事，唯魏帝為紀，其功臣及吳、蜀之主，並皆為傳，仍各依其國，部類相從，謂之《三國志》。

translations.literal: In Jin times, Chen Shou of Ba commandery edited and compiled the affairs of the Three Kingdoms: only the Wei emperor received annals, while meritorious ministers and the rulers of Wu and Shu were all given biographies; still arranged by state and category, the work was called the Records of the Three Kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times, Chen Shou of Ba commandery edited and compiled the affairs of the Three Kingdoms: only the Wei emperor received annals, while meritorious ministers and the rulers of Wu and Shu were all given biographies; still arranged by state and category, the work was called the Records of the Three Kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 壽卒後，梁州大中正範穎表奏其事，帝詔河南尹、洛陽令，就壽家寫之。

translations.literal: Shou卒後, Provincial Rectifier of Liang Province範穎表奏其事, 帝詔河Nan尹、Magistrate of Luoyang, 就Shou家寫之。.
translations.idiomatic: Shou卒後, Provincial Rectifier of Liang Province範穎表奏其事, 帝詔河Nan尹、Magistrate of Luoyang, 就Shou家寫之。.

sentences.zh: 自是世有著述，皆擬班、馬，以為正史，作者尤廣。

translations.literal: From this time onward there were authors of historical works everywhere, all taking Ban Gu and Sima Qian as models and treating their works as standard histories; authors became especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward there were authors of historical works everywhere, all taking Ban Gu and Sima Qian as models and treating their works as standard histories; authors became especially numerous.

translations.literal: Histories of a single dynasty numbered as many as several dozen schools.
translations.idiomatic: Histories of a single dynasty numbered as many as several dozen schools.

sentences.zh: 唯《史記》、《漢書》，師法相傳，並有解釋。

translations.literal: Only the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han were handed down from master to pupil, and both had explanatory commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han were handed down from master to pupil, and both had explanatory commentaries.

sentences.zh: 《三國志》及范曄《後漢》，雖有音注，既近世之作，並讀之可知。

translations.literal: The Records of the Three Kingdoms and Fan Ye's Book of Later Han, though they have pronunciation guides and commentaries, are recent works and can be understood upon reading.
translations.idiomatic: The Records of the Three Kingdoms and Fan Ye's Book of Later Han, though they have pronunciation guides and commentaries, are recent works and can be understood upon reading.

sentences.zh: 梁時，明《漢書》有劉顯、韋棱，陳時有姚察，隋代有包愷、蕭該，並為名家。

translations.literal: In Liang times those who mastered the Book of Han included Liu Xian and Wei Leng; in Chen times there was Yao Cha; in Sui times there were Bao Kai and Xiao Gai—all were renowned masters.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang times those who mastered the Book of Han included Liu Xian and Wei Leng; in Chen times there was Yao Cha; in Sui times there were Bao Kai and Xiao Gai—all were renowned masters.

translations.literal: Transmitters of the Records of the Grand Historian were very few.
translations.idiomatic: Transmitters of the Records of the Grand Historian were very few.

sentences.zh: 今依其世代，聚而編之，以備正史。

translations.literal: Now, arranged by period, they are gathered and compiled to supplement the standard histories.
translations.idiomatic: Now, arranged by period, they are gathered and compiled to supplement the standard histories.

translations.literal: Since the historiographers were abolished, successive authors all took Ban Gu and Sima Qian as their standard.
translations.idiomatic: Since the historiographers were abolished, successive authors all took Ban Gu and Sima Qian as their standard.

sentences.zh: 起漢獻帝，雅好典籍，以班固《漢書》文繁難省，命潁川荀悅作《春秋左傳》之體，為《漢紀》三十篇。

translations.literal: Beginning with Emperor Xian of Han, who greatly loved the classics, finding Ban Gu's Book of Han too verbose and hard to abridge, he ordered Xun Yue of Yingchuan to compose in the style of the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn, producing the Annals of Han in thirty chapters.

sentences.zh: 言約而事詳，辯論多美，大行於世。

translations.literal: Its words were concise yet its events detailed, its arguments often elegant, and it circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Its words were concise yet its events detailed, its arguments often elegant, and it circulated widely in the world.

sentences.zh: 至晉太康元年，汲郡人發魏襄王塚，得古竹簡書，字皆科斗。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Taikang era of Jin, a man of Ji commandery excavated the tomb of King Xiang of Wei and obtained ancient bamboo-slip books written in tadpole script.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Taikang era of Jin, a man of Ji commandery excavated the tomb of King Xiang of Wei and obtained ancient bamboo-slip books written in tadpole script.

sentences.zh: 發塚者不以為意，往往散亂。

translations.literal: The excavators paid them no heed, and they were often scattered and disordered.
translations.idiomatic: The excavators paid them no heed, and they were often scattered and disordered.

sentences.zh: 帝命中書監荀勖、令和嶠，撰次為十五部，八十七卷。

translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Xun Xu, Director of the Secretariat, and He Qiao, Director of the Masters of Writing, to arrange them into fifteen sections in eighty-seven scrolls.

sentences.zh: 多雜碎怪妄，不可訓知，唯《周易》、《紀年》，最為分了。

translations.literal: Much was miscellaneous, fragmentary, strange, and absurd, and could not be reliably understood; only the Book of Changes and the Chronological Annals were most clearly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Much was miscellaneous, fragmentary, strange, and absurd, and could not be reliably understood; only the Book of Changes and the Chronological Annals were most clearly distinguished.

sentences.zh: 其《周易》上下篇，與今正同。

translations.literal: Its upper and lower sections of the Book of Changes are exactly the same as the present text.
translations.idiomatic: Its upper and lower sections of the Book of Changes are exactly the same as the present text.

sentences.zh: 《紀年》皆用夏正建寅之月為歲首，起自夏、殷、周三代王事，無諸侯國別。

translations.literal: The Chronological Annals all use the first month of the Xia calendar, establishing yin as the year's beginning; they begin with the royal affairs of the Xia, Yin, and Zhou Three Dynasties, without distinction among feudal states.
translations.idiomatic: The Chronological Annals all use the first month of the Xia calendar, establishing yin as the year's beginning; they begin with the royal affairs of the Xia, Yin, and Zhou Three Dynasties, without distinction among feudal states.

sentences.zh: 唯特記晉國，起自稱殤叔，次文侯、昭侯，以至曲沃莊伯，盡晉國滅。

translations.literal: They specially record the state of Jin, beginning with the one called Shang Shu, then Marquis Wen, Marquis Zhao, down to Zhuang Bo of Quwo, ending with the destruction of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: They specially record the state of Jin, beginning with the one called Shang Shu, then Marquis Wen, Marquis Zhao, down to Zhuang Bo of Quwo, ending with the destruction of Jin.

sentences.zh: 獨記魏事，下至魏哀王，謂之「今王」。

translations.literal: They record Wei affairs alone, down to King Ai of Wei, whom they call "the present king."
translations.idiomatic: They record Wei affairs alone, down to King Ai of Wei, whom they call "the present king."
